web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Reverse DCF, Cash Leaks & Peer Multiples
question: What Henry Hub strip, PipeBox cash sweeps, and Range merger dilution are priced into EQT at $48.89?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. In commodities, headline free cash flow flatters the stock whenever prior claims sit ahead of common shareholders.
epigraph.author: Howard Marks, The Most Important Thing (paraphrased)

web_blocks.title: Headline multiples versus the enterprise value bridge

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $48.89, EQT carries a $30.58B market cap on 625.55M shares [23, 24]. Enterprise value stands at $39.61B after $5.51B of net debt ($5.59B total debt principal less ~$0.08B cash) and ~$3.52B of PipeBox non-controlling interest [24, 29]. Trailing multiples look modest on paper: 11.59x trailing P/E, 6.03x EV/EBITDA, 8.02x P/FCF, and 1.20x price-to-book [23, 24]. Yet forward P/E climbs to 14.55x as consensus EPS is projected to drop 9.95% next year [24]. Two drivers explain that compression: weaker 2027 natural gas pricing and upcoming equity dilution from the Range Resources merger [26, 38].

web_blocks.title: What $48.89 implies in a reverse discounted cash flow model

web_blocks.html: A reverse DCF translates a stock price into the steady-state cash flow buyers must assume to earn their cost of capital. With the 10-year U.S. Treasury yielding 5.04% on November 19, 2026, a cyclical gas producer requires at least a 9.0% WACC [39]. Pairing a 9.0% discount rate with 2.0% terminal growth means a $39.61B enterprise value prices in $2.72B of annual unlevered free cash flow forever. Compare that hurdle against EQT's actual 2027 cash outlook under the November 10 EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook [38]. The EIA cut its 2027 Henry Hub forecast by 8.8% to $2.88/MMBtu (and Winter Nov–Mar by 16% to $2.87/MMBtu) as U.S. crude reaches 14.3 MMb/d and associated Permian gas keeps expanding [38].

Footnote forensics from Pass 1 change the equity math materially at $2.88/MMBtu gas. On ~2,450 Bcfe of standalone output above EQT's ~$2.00/MMBtu unlevered breakeven, $2.88/MMBtu Henry Hub generates roughly $1.85B in consolidated FCF [5, 38]. However, Note 9 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q discloses that Blackstone's PipeBox joint venture sweeps 60% of available midstream cash flow to Blackstone ($355.1M paid in 9M 2026, or ~$473M annualized) until ~$3.3B of remaining Base Return is satisfied [29]. Deducting ~$450M of annual PipeBox distributions leaves only ~$1.40B of 2027 standalone FCF attributable to EQT equity holders. On a $30.58B market cap, that equals a 4.58% normalized FCF yield—46 bps below the risk-free 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield [24, 39].

web_blocks.the_number: Pro forma Base Case fair value is $50.00 per share (Bear $31.22; Bull $66.00). At $48.89, normalized 2027 attributable FCF yields 4.58% standalone and 5.13% pro forma.
web_blocks.how_calculated: We model pro forma EQT plus Range EBITDA across three gas regimes. Next, we subtract $10.43B of net debt and PipeBox NCI ($5.51B EQT, $1.40B Range, $3.52B PipeBox). Finally, we divide by 856.6M pro forma shares and benchmark attributable FCF against the 5.04% 10Y Treasury.

Balance sheet inputs include $5.59B debt, PipeBox's 60% cash sweep (~$3.3B remaining), $13.2B pipe commitments, $2.50/Dth short puts, and a $1,148M HSR break-up fee.

Base sits at $50.00 (~$3.00 above-strip gas, $7.7B EBITDA at 6.9x HSR-ceiling multiple); Bull reaches $66.00 ($3.65 gas, $600M synergies, $9.5B EBITDA at 7.05x).

An FTC block removes 231M dilution shares. However, it triggers a $1,148M ($1.84/share) reverse break-up fee.

web_blocks.title: Hidden cash drains, collar asymmetry, and Range HSR risk

web_blocks.html: Three structural frictions keep EQT's valuation capped near $50.00—and note that $50.00 already embeds above-strip $3.00/MMBtu gas (vs. $2.88 EIA strip, worth $39.67) and a near-ceiling 6.9x HSR multiple [31, 38]. First, EQT carries $13.2B of off-balance-sheet pipeline commitments (~$1.1B/year in 2026–2027) and $590M in 2028 LNG ship leases [29, 30]. Those fixed demand charges continue even during curtailments, squeezing unit margins when volumes drop [29, 30]. Second, EQT shifted its 2027 hedge book (462 MMDth) to 49% fixed swaps at $3.13–$3.16/Dth and 51% three-way collars with sold $2.50/Dth puts [29]. Upside is capped on half the hedged book, while downside reopens below $2.50/Dth after $191M in 9M basis hedge losses [29]. Sensitivity remains high: each $0.25/MMBtu move swings pro forma cash flow by ~$700M (~$0.82/share), or ~$0.65/share attributable FCF after a ~20% tax and PipeBox NCI deduction [29].

Third, the Range Resources merger entered federal Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) antitrust review on November 20, 2026 [31, 36]. Because the combined firm controls ~25% of Marcellus supply, regulators may demand divestitures or delay closing toward April 25, 2028 [31, 36]. Worse, EQT owes Range an asymmetric $1,148M reverse break-up fee if clearance fails, nearly triple Range's $423M fee [31]. Adding Range's ~$1.4B net debt puts ~$10.43B of senior claims ahead of 856.6M combined shares [26, 29, 31].

web_blocks.takeaway: At $48.89, EQT trades well above its $39.67 EIA $2.88/MMBtu strip value ($7.05B at 6.3x). Our $50.00 Base Case already assumes above-strip $3.00 gas and a near-ceiling 6.9x HSR multiple, while Bear ($6.3B at 5.9x) math yields $31.22 [24, 29, 38].

web_blocks.title: Benchmarking EQT against live energy peers

web_blocks.html: Comparing EQT against listed peers in our November 20 snapshot shows why the market withholds a midstream multiple. Antero Resources (AR) trades at 8.06x P/E and 6.20x P/FCF with 11.15% ROIC, yet sits in Stage 4 [23, 24]. Permian Resources (PR) trades at 11.05x P/E with 10.60% ROIC and also holds Stage 4 [23, 24]. Meanwhile, LNG exporter Cheniere (LNG) earns 20.56x P/E in Stage 2 because fee contracts shield cash flow [23, 24]. Until EQT retires PipeBox's $3.3B Base Return and closes Range, its 8.56% ROIC trails our 9.0% WACC [24, 29].

web_blocks.takeaway: All three U.S. upstream producers in our snapshot (EQT, AR, PR) sit in Stage 4 Markdown with sub-12x P/Es. By contrast, contracted LNG exporter Cheniere (LNG) trades at 20.56x P/E in Stage 2 because fee contracts shield cash flow [23, 24].

web_blocks.mechanism: Prior to forming Expand Energy, Southwestern Energy traded at 5x–6x EV/EBITDA during sub-$3.00/MMBtu gas strips. Market debate centered on merger synergies, FTC HSR delays, and take-or-pay pipe commitments.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Southwestern shares stayed range-bound between $5.50 and $7.50 for over 18 months during the 2024 FTC review. Shares only broke higher after gas strips cleared $3.25/MMBtu and merger close removed deal arbitrage.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Low-cost gas consolidators rarely re-rate above 6.5x–7.0x EV/EBITDA during federal HSR review. Forward Henry Hub strips below $3.00/MMBtu keep multiples compressed.

book_paragraphs: Open any brokerage screen on November 20, 2026, look at EQT Corporation at $48.89, and your first instinct might be to call it a bargain. After all, trailing P/E sits at 11.59x, EV-to-EBITDA reads 6.03x, and trailing price-to-free-cash-flow looks like an enticing 8.02x [23, 24]. Yet value traps in commodity industries almost always wear cheap trailing multiples at the exact moment forward cash flows compress.

To strip away that trailing illusion, let us run a reverse discounted cash flow model from the $48.89 close. With 625.55 million standalone shares, $5.51 billion in net debt, and roughly $3.52 billion of Blackstone PipeBox non-controlling interest, EQT carries an enterprise value of $39.61 billion [24, 29]. Meanwhile, the risk-free 10-year U.S. Treasury yield sits at 5.04% [39]. Demanding a realistic 9.0% cost of capital and 2.0% terminal growth means today's $39.61 billion enterprise value assumes EQT generates $2.72 billion of steady-state unlevered free cash flow every year.

Now test that $2.72 billion requirement against the fresh November 10, 2026 Energy Information Administration forecast and our Pass 1 footnote audit. The EIA cut its 2027 Henry Hub forecast by 8.8% to $2.88 per MMBtu—and chopped its November-through-March winter forecast by 16% to $2.87 per MMBtu—because U.S. crude oil production climbing toward 14.3 million barrels per day keeps flooding the grid with associated Permian gas [38].

At $2.88 per MMBtu Henry Hub, EQT's standalone wells still clear their ~$2.00 breakeven and generate roughly $1.85 billion of consolidated free cash flow. Here is where Note 9 of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q changes the verdict: Blackstone's PipeBox joint venture sweeps 60% of available midstream cash flow to Blackstone until Blackstone collects another $3.3 billion in Base Return—draining $355.1 million in the first nine months of 2026 alone [29]. Subtract roughly $450 million per year of PipeBox cash distributions, and standalone attributable free cash flow drops to ~$1.40 billion. Divided by $30.58 billion of equity value, that is a 4.58% normalized cash yield—46 basis points below what you can earn risk-free in 10-year U.S. Treasuries [24, 39].

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a cyclical natural gas producer yields 4.58% on normalized 2027 attributable free cash flow while a risk-free 10-year Treasury pays 5.04%, equity investors are paying for upside that has not arrived yet.

book_subsections.title: Pro Forma Range Resources Math: Dilution, Net Debt & The $1,148M Break-Up Fee
paragraphs: Management pitches the Range Resources acquisition as a cure-all that adds 2.50 Bcfe/d of liquids-rich production and $325 million of initial synergies [26]. Let us verify the pro forma enterprise bridge carefully rather than accepting a presentation slide. At the 0.987x exchange ratio, EQT will issue roughly 231 million new shares, taking diluted share count to ~856.6 million [26]. Combined senior claims ahead of common stock reach ~$10.43 billion: EQT's $5.51 billion net debt, ~$1.40 billion of Range net debt, and ~$3.52 billion for Blackstone's PipeBox stake [26, 29].

At $2.88 per MMBtu gas in 2027, combined pro forma EBITDA lands near $7.05 billion, and attributable free cash flow after PipeBox sweeps reaches ~$2.15 billion—a 5.13% yield on $41.88 billion of pro forma equity value, or a razor-thin 9 basis points above 10-year Treasuries [38, 39]. Worse, Range's November 20, 2026 Form 425 confirmed that federal Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust review has begun [36]. Because the merged company controls roughly 25% of Marcellus gas output, regulators could demand divestitures or block the deal—triggering an asymmetric $1,148 million reverse break-up fee owed by EQT, equivalent to $1.84 per standalone share [31].

book_subsections.title: Why Off-Balance-Sheet Pipes and Three-Way Collars Matter at $2.88 Gas
paragraphs: Two additional footnotes keep our Base Case fair value capped at $50.00 per share rather than the prior $64.00 estimate. First, EQT carries $13.2 billion of off-balance-sheet firm pipeline and processing commitments—about $1.1 billion per year in 2026 and 2027—alongside $590 million in 2028 LNG vessel leases [29, 30]. Those take-or-pay bills keep running even when management curtails wells during weak summer pricing, turning volume discipline into fixed-cost drag [29, 30].

Second, Q3 2026 disclosures show EQT shifted its 2027 hedge book to 228 MMDth of fixed swaps at $3.13–$3.16 per Dth and 234 MMDth of three-way collars with sold $2.50 per Dth puts [29]. If associated Permian gas pushes Henry Hub below $2.50, EQT loses downside protection dollar-for-dollar, while upside above $3.16 is capped on nearly half its hedged volume [29]. Note too that each $0.25 per MMBtu shift alters pro forma cash flow by roughly $700 million (~$0.82 per share pre-tax across 856.6 million shares), or ~$0.65 per share of attributable free cash flow after a ~20% cash-tax and PipeBox NCI deduction [29]. Put all of those pieces together: Base Case fair value at above-strip $3.00 gas and an upper-end 6.9x HSR-review multiple is $50.00 per share (vs. $39.67 at EIA's $2.88 strip), Bear Case ($6.3B EBITDA at 5.9x) calculates to $31.22, and Bull Case reaches $66.00.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Peer Table: Why Upstream Gas Stays Cheap
paragraphs: Look across our November 20, 2026 live peer snapshot. Antero Resources trades at 8.06x trailing P/E and 6.20x P/FCF with an 11.15% return on invested capital—yet sits in Stage 4 Markdown at $35.67 [23, 24]. Permian Resources trades at 11.05x trailing P/E with 10.60% ROIC and also sits in Stage 4 at $21.15 [23, 24]. Only Cheniere Energy (LNG), whose long-term liquefaction fees insulate cash flows from domestic oversupply, holds Stage 2 at 20.56x P/E [23, 24].

The lesson is identical to the 2023–2024 Southwestern Energy merger cycle. When forward gas sits below $3.00 per MMBtu and federal antitrust review hangs over a mega-merger, upstream consolidators trade at 6x to 7x EBITDA regardless of rock quality. Next, Chapter 8 inspects the live November 20 chart to see whether institutional buyers are stepping in or stepping aside.

book_subsections.title: Comparing Risk-Free Treasuries Against Commodity Equity Risk
paragraphs: Before you ever buy a cyclical stock, run one simple sanity check: compare its normalized free cash flow yield against the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield. On November 19, 2026, risk-free 10-year Treasuries paid 5.04% [39]. That yield requires zero drilling risk, zero pipeline take-or-pay exposure, and zero antitrust risk.

By contrast, at $48.89 per share and the EIA's $2.88 per MMBtu 2027 Henry Hub forecast, EQT offers only 4.58% standalone attributable free cash flow yield—and 5.13% on a pro forma combined basis after Blackstone takes its 60% PipeBox distribution [29, 38]. Taking commodity volatility and merger execution risk for nine basis points over Treasuries makes no sense. Demand at least a 250-to-300 basis point cash-yield cushion—above 7.5%—before committing fresh capital to a gas producer.
